remaining.classification: equivalent under local rootChanged invariant
remaining.reason: rootChanged becomes true only after the requested root row was found and assigned to the local root variable. That local variable is not cleared by callbacks or awaits. The following root!==undefined check is therefore true whenever reached with rootChanged, under the current method control flow.

remaining.classification: same result with extra null-parent query
remaining.reason: If the root has no parent but has a command sequence, bypassing the parent-identity guard performs a SELECT with a null parent ID, then the parent!==undefined guard skips notification. Output is unchanged but query work and failure observations differ. With ordinary paired metadata, the command-sequence guard already skips parentless roots. Keep the cheap guard; this is not strict I/O equivalence.

remaining.classification: deferred root-result semantics with newly open descendants
remaining.reason: The boolean reports whether the selected root changed. Current repeated-cancellation cases have no newly open child. If an already cancelling parent later schedules a compensation child, traversal can change only that descendant; this mutation would incorrectly report a root change. Add a public compensation/child scenario and clarify repeated propagation semantics across adapters rather than assume the return guard is equivalent.

remaining.classification: defensive admission reconciliation under pending-state invariant
remaining.reason: A pending execution owns no retained permit, and supported serialized memory admission transitions already fill newly available capacity. Its releaseConcurrency call normally reasserts false and reconciles an already full key, so the pending cancellation output is unchanged without it. External/test-seam state transitions can leave reconcilable capacity; keep this defense and do not generalize equivalence to arbitrary manipulated states.

scorePolicy: Keep 31 survivors,1 uncovered default and6 timeouts visible. No exclusions, no blanket equivalence and no blocking threshold. TypeScript AST mutation does not systematically mutate SQL predicates or prove transaction interleavings.
reviewAgainWhen: Prioritize direct-child termination under a terminal parent, repeated cancellation after compensation child creation, then partial/orphan/cyclic low-level graph contracts and shared-schema multi-connection races.
